title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## RPG: Guided Self‑Improvement for Embodied Agents

### The Breakthrough
RPG lets robots close skill gaps without changing model weights: it diagnoses failures from simulator state and execution feedback, generates new symbolic skills and updates an LLM‑driven prompt, then practices in simulation. Across 22 held‑out manipulation tasks success climbs from 28.6% after one round to 95.0% after 15 rounds, beating ASPIRE (75.5%) and CaP‑Agent0 (60.0%). After a standard calibration, the frozen system solves all 30 real‑world trials (10 per task).

### The Caveats
The self‑improvement loop is demonstrated on only three manipulation tasks, so broader generalisation remains unverified.

## Self‑Organizing Spiking Neural Network Walks Robot Dog

### The Breakthrough
A robot dog learns to walk using a spiking neural network that self‑organizes motor patterns via intrinsic plasticity, encoding proprioceptive feedback into spike trains and requiring no external reward signal. The SNN discovers stable gait cycles autonomously and achieves sustained walking in its test environment.

### The Caveats
The demo is unverified beyond a Hacker News post and lacks formal evaluation or baseline comparisons.

## GlassGuard: Verified Glass Plane Mapping

### The Breakthrough
GlassGuard fuses foundation‑model glass instance masks with LiDAR cues, generates metric plane hypotheses and applies depth‑free projective checks, yielding 85% panoramic glass coverage (82% with pinhole inputs) and reducing false voxels by 5‑17× per frame compared to reported baselines.

### The Caveats
Baseline methods are unnamed and undescribed, preventing a clear assessment of the claimed improvement.

## HumanoidToolBench Benchmark for Tool Use

### The Breakthrough
HumanoidToolBench introduces an 18‑task benchmark that evaluates tool selection, manipulation and locomotion, backed by the ToolBook dataset of 3.1 k demos collected in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 robot, revealing large drops in performance on unseen tools and unrelated instructions.

### The Caveats
No prior baselines are reported, so the benchmark’s difficulty relative to existing methods is unclear.

## SkeleWAM Skeleton‑Based Manipulation Model

### The Breakthrough
SkeleWAM builds an online 3D skeleton from RGB‑D and proprioception, uses Medoid Action Consensus to refine stochastic action samples, and with only 57.1 M parameters attains 85.9% success on the LIBERO‑Plus benchmark, surpassing Cosmos‑Policy by 3.7 points.

### The Caveats
Results are confined to simulation; real‑robot transfer has not been demonstrated.

## Kolibri Open‑Weight German/English LLM

### The Breakthrough
Kolibri is a 78 B‑parameter mixture‑of‑experts LLM (50 layers, 384 experts per layer, routing each token to 6 experts) that runs at ~3.5 B FLOPs per token, achieves 87.5% on the German AIME benchmark and supports up to 1 M‑token contexts via sliding‑window attention.

### The Caveats
Performance is shown only on synthetic language benchmarks, with no robotic or hardware experiments.

## Robot Harness C++17 Execution Framework

### The Breakthrough
Robot Harness is an open‑source C++17 library that links embodied AI agents, robot skills and environments through three safety checks, provides ROS2 Nav2 and Gazebo integration, and demonstrates composable, interruptible actions with demo result sums of 29 and 61.

### The Caveats
The framework is evaluated only in Gazebo and lacks comparison to existing robot runtimes, leaving its claimed advantages unverified.

### Priority
RPG showcases a weight‑free self‑improvement loop that achieves near‑perfect real‑world manipulation performance, making it the most actionable breakthrough for today’s robotics teams.

### One action
Consider adding a failure‑diagnosis and symbolic‑skill generation module to your frozen LLM‑driven manipulation pipeline to replicate RPG’s self‑improvement gains.

### What to watch
RPG, SkeleWAM and HumanoidToolBench all target manipulation improvement—RPG with real‑world self‑practice, SkeleWAM with a compact skeleton representation in simulation, and HumanoidToolBench providing a new benchmark that stresses tool selection and locomotion. Progress across these strands will reveal whether simulation‑centric efficiency (SkeleWAM) or autonomous practice loops (RPG) can close the gaps highlighted by the benchmark.
